GATE-DOWN-1 — lower the pre-launch gate, right now, without a deploy.
19 Aug 2026 · David's ruling · reversible in one command (printed at the end of the run)

WHY THIS ROUTE: the deploy lane is not reaching the server, so this deliberately does not
depend on it. It is an nginx-only change and carries its own backup, config test and
auto-restore. It touches nothing in the application.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STEP 1 — paste this ONE block into a terminal (it SSHes in and runs the change):
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ssh root@trustsquare.co "echo  | base64 -d > /tmp/026_gate_down.py && python3 /tmp/026_gate_down.py --apply"

(If your SSH alias is different, swap root@trustsquare.co for whatever
 deploy_marketsquare.bat uses as %SERVER%.)

It prints, in order: the site file it found, the backup path, "nginx -t ok", and then
either GATE IS DOWN or a refusal explaining exactly what it would not guess at.
If anything fails it restores the backup itself — the gate stays up rather than
half-changed.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STEP 2 — prove it from anywhere (no cookie, no code):
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

curl -s  https://trustsquare.co/review/verify     ->  {"valid":true,"scope":"review"}
curl -sI https://trustsquare.co/listings          ->  HTTP/2 200      (was 401)

Then just open https://trustsquare.co in a private window. No gate screen should appear.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STEP 3 — while you are on the box, grab the deploy log (the other blocker):
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ssh root@trustsquare.co "tail -40 /var/log/marketsquare-deploy.log; echo ---; systemctl status marketsquare-deploy.timer --no-pager | head -20"

Paste that output back and I will tell you why deploys stopped landing.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TO PUT THE GATE BACK (real rollback, nothing was deleted):
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The run prints the exact command, of the form:
  cp /root/nginx-site-backups/<file>.bak-gatedown-<timestamp> /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/<file> && nginx -t && nginx -s reload

Cookies people already hold keep working either way.
